newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong urges calm after islands protester dies.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong urges calm after islands protester dies.

text.p: Hong Kong appealed for calm on Thursday after a Hong Kong protest leader drowned while campaigning for Chinese sovereignty over a disputed group of East China Sea islands.
"This has been distressing for us, and I appeal for calm from all," Home Affairs Secretary Michael Suen said in a statement.
"I urge the community to react to this development in...an orderly and responsible manner."

David Chan, the leader of a group of 18 activists on board the protest ship Kien Hwa 2, died on Thursday after leaping off the bow of the vessel in defiance of a blockade of the islands by Japanese coastguard vessels.
Chan and four other protesters who jumped with him had tied themselves to the ship and were dragged along in the wake of the vessel.
One of the other four was injured and flown to a hospital in the Japanese prefecture of Okinawa. The other three were plucked from the sea unhurt.

Hong Kong has been swept by Chinese nationalistic fervour for weeks since rightist extremists planted symbols of Japanese sovereignty on the islands known to the Chinese as the Diaoyus and to Japanese as the Senkakus.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule next year.

Japan has claimed sovereign rights to the islands and refused to acknowledge that the dispute is still open for discussion with China. Tokyo's claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
